bridge: Start with the company: its employees’ own gifts, and its PAC’s.
how: Each dot is one member serving on Nov. 26, 2026.

head: At the end of 2024, 10 members now serving had received money from Anthropic’s employees or its PAC. By Sept. 30, 2026: 197.
deck: The employees gave their own money: $5.9M, 92% of it dated 2026. The company’s PAC made its first gift on record to a member now serving on June 29, 2026; by Sept. 30 it had given $200K to 81 members, 17 of whom had no gift from an employee.
note: A person’s contribution is their own money, not their employer’s. Employer is as the giver reported it to the FEC. Both counts are of the members serving on Nov. 26, 2026; the record stops at Sept. 30, 2026.
bridge: $6.1M in all. The large money moved another way.
source: Source: FEC contribution records in this project’s tables: contributions to the campaign, leadership PAC or single-member joint fundraising committee of a serving member, through Sept. 30, 2026; ANTHROPAC is Anthropic PBC’s political action committee.

head: Anthropic announced $40.0M for Public First Action. There the trail stops: no filing in this record lists the group’s donors.
deck: Separate FEC filings show receipts from Public First Action at 6 committees. The largest spending total for one candidate was $15.0M for Alexander Bores, outside Congress.
note: In the 2020, 2022 and 2024 election cycles, Dustin Moskovitz gave $100M to Future Forward (FF PAC).
bridge: Another kind of giving reaches more members: lobbyists’ own gifts.
source: Sources include Anthropic’s announcements and FEC receipt and outside-spending filings.

head: Lobbyists’ own gifts reach the most members: $1.8M went to campaigns or committees linked to 356 serving members.
note: The gift is the lobbyist’s own money. The record does not say why it was made. Named lobbyists only: $1.3M in 1,022 gifts.
bridge: Anthropic’s own lobbying is on a different record. What did the company report?
how: Counted: a gift whose giver was a registered lobbyist at a firm that had a network client in that period. Each lit seat has a campaign or committee linked to a gift.
source: Lobbyists’ semi-annual contribution reports to Congress. Gifts dated Feb. 19, 2021 to June 30, 2026. Filed recipient names, and committee records where the filing gives them, identify the member for each counted gift.

head: In the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic reported $5.6M in lobbying expenses, more than $3.1M in all of 2025.
deck: Which bills did the lobbying reports name?
bridge: The gifts and the lobbying are recent. Who was Congress hearing from before them?
source: Sources include quarterly lobbying reports through Sept. 30, 2026, official bill records and federal contribution filings.

head: Congress heard from Georgetown’s CSET in 2019.
source: Sources · Congressional witness lists and transcripts, the funder’s published grant list and IRS Form 990 grant schedules.

head: Horizon placed 25 fellows in Congress.
deck: Horizon says each host manages its fellow’s work.
note: The Horizon Institute for Public Service is the listed recipient of $11.9M in network grants. It also has other funders.
bridge: What is on file for each member?
source: Sources · Horizon’s roster and host guidance, and grant records. The sheet also uses alumni pages, congressional records, filings and staff pages.

head: A record of ties, not a record of influence.
deck: 240 of the 452 members with a tie have one or two kinds of record. The record reaches Democrats and Republicans at similar rates, with third-party-only records making up a larger share of counted Republicans.
how: Members serving on Nov. 26, 2026, by party. Records through Sept. 30, 2026.
